# `silk/compress/brotli_encode`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compress bytes as Brotli streams (RFC 7932), in steps or all at once, with qualities 0 to 11.

## When to use
Use a [`BrotliEncoder`](#BrotliEncoder) to write `.br` files or HTTP bodies with `Content-Encoding: br`, in
steps and with fixed memory. Use [`BrotliEncoder.encode`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.encode) to compress one complete buffer.
Decode with `silk.compress.brotli.Brotli`.

## Details
Up to quality 9 the encoder finds matches with the bucket hash tables of the reference
`brotli` (more and longer buckets as the quality rises), checks the recent distances first, and
looks one or more bytes ahead for a better match from quality 2. Qualities 10 and 11 collect
all matches from a binary tree and choose the commands with the shortest path search of the
reference, priced by estimated literal costs, and at quality 11 a second time with the costs of
the first result. They also copy words of the static dictionary, with the transforms that keep
the start of the word, and pick the postfix bits and direct codes of the distances. Each
meta-block gets its own prefix codes for literals, commands, and distances. From quality 5 the
literals use one prefix code for each cluster of the 64 contexts of their two previous bytes,
in UTF-8 or signed context mode. A meta-block that does not shrink is stored uncompressed.
[`BrotliEncoder.make`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.make) allocates all storage one time. Later calls do not allocate and do not
keep a borrow of your buffers. The output is deterministic but is not the same bytes that the
reference `brotli` writes.

## Examples
### Compress a buffer
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.compress.brotli_encode { BrotliEncodeError, BrotliEncoder, BrotliOptions }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError | BrotliEncodeError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let input = b"abcabcabcabcabcabcabcabcabcabcabcabc"
  let mut output: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
  let written = run BrotliEncoder.encode(input, &mut output, BrotliOptions.make(5))
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if written == 0 || written >= input.length {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `BrotliEncoder` with `import silk.compress.brotli_encode { BrotliEncoder }`.

<a id="BrotliEncodeError"></a>

## `BrotliEncodeError`

```silk
pub struct BrotliEncodeError
```

An encoding failure, with the progress of the call before it failed.

### Gotchas
After a failed [`BrotliEncoder.step`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.step), discard the stream. Each later step fails with
`InvalidUse` until you call [`BrotliEncoder.reset`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.reset).

## `BrotliOptions`


The settings of a [`BrotliEncoder`](#BrotliEncoder).

<a id="BrotliOptions.quality"></a>

### Field `quality`

```silk
pub quality: u32
```

The effort, from 0 to 11. 0 is the fastest and 11 the smallest. The reference `brotli`
defaults to 11.

<a id="BrotliOptions.windowBits"></a>

### Field `windowBits`

```silk
pub windowBits: u32
```

The base-2 logarithm of the window, from 10 to 24. Matches reach back up to the window size
less 16 bytes. The stream header records it, and the decoder needs a window of that size.

<a id="BrotliEncoder"></a>

## `BrotliEncoder`

```silk
pub struct BrotliEncoder
```

A streaming Brotli encoder that owns its window, match tables, and output buffer.

### When to use
Use it to compress data that arrives in parts, as the reference `BrotliEncoderCompressStream`
does. Make one with [`BrotliEncoder.make`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.make), call [`BrotliEncoder.step`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.step) with each part of the
input, and end with `BrotliFlush.End`. Call [`BrotliEncoder.reset`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.reset) to write another stream
with the same storage.

### Details
[`BrotliEncoder.make`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.make) allocates all storage one time: twice the window or twice the
meta-block (64 KiB to 256 KiB), whichever is larger, and about two meta-blocks of command and
output buffers. Up to quality 9 it adds the hash buckets (512 KiB at quality 0 and 32 MiB at 9,
less when the window is small), and from quality 5 about 300 KiB for literal contexts.
Qualities 10 and 11 add one more window, a binary tree of 8 bytes for each byte of the window,
about 17 MiB for matches and the shortest path search, and 200 KiB for a dictionary index.
Later calls do not allocate and do not keep a borrow of your buffers, so you can move the
encoder between threads between calls.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError | BrotliEncodeError

```

Returns an encoder for one stream with `options`, with storage from the ambient `Allocator`.

#### Errors
- [`BrotliEncodeError`](#BrotliEncodeError) with `InvalidOptions` if the quality is above 11 or the window bits
  are not 10 to 24, checked before the allocation.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="BrotliEncoder.impl.step"></a>

### Method `step`

```silk
pub fn step(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], flush: BrotliFlush) -> Result<
    BrotliEncodeProgress,
    BrotliEncodeError,
  >
```

Compresses from `input` into `output` and returns how much it consumed and wrote.

#### Details
On the next call, give only the input after the consumed prefix. You can give a new output
buffer of any length. Call with `BrotliFlush.Continue` while more input follows. A flush
finishes only when the step returns `Flushed`, or `Finished` for `BrotliFlush.End`. Until
then, call again with the same flush. A flush that has to pad the stream to a whole byte
writes an empty metadata meta-block, as the reference `brotli` does.

#### Errors
`InvalidUse` with input after the stream finished, or after an earlier failure.

<a id="BrotliEncoder.impl.encodedBound"></a>

### Associated function `encodedBound`

```silk
pub fn encodedBound(length: usize) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the most bytes that [`BrotliEncoder.encode`](#BrotliEncoder.impl.encode) can write for `length` input bytes with
any options, or `None` if that count does not fit in `usize`.

#### Details
An output buffer of this size never fails with `OutputFull`. The bound is the input, 5
bytes of header and padding for each 64 KiB meta-block or part of one, and 3 bytes for the
stream header, its end, and the last padding.

<a id="BrotliEncoder.impl.encode"></a>

### Associated function `encode`

```silk
pub effect fn encode(input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], options: BrotliOptions) -> usize
    ! OutOfMemoryError | BrotliEncodeError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Compresses all of `input` into the start of `output` as one stream with `options`, and
returns the encoded length.

#### Details
It makes a [`BrotliEncoder`](#BrotliEncoder) with storage from the ambient `Allocator`, runs one step with
`BrotliFlush.End`, and releases the storage before it returns. The window shrinks to the
smallest one, at least 10 bits, whose reach holds the input, so small inputs need little
memory and the decoder needs a small window.

#### Errors
- `OutputFull` if `output` fills before the stream is complete. It never occurs when `output`
  holds at least `BrotliEncoder.encodedBound(input.length)` bytes. Discard the partial stream.
- `InvalidOptions` if an option is outside its range.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
